Recall the vector pairs: displacement links to velocity, while distance links to speed, and check which pairing statement D uses.

walkthrough: Identify what is asked: find the single statement about velocity, displacement, distance and acceleration that is false.
Recall the definitions: velocity $v = \Delta s / \Delta t$ where $s$ is displacement, speed $= \Delta d / \Delta t$ where $d$ is distance, and acceleration $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$.

Check the graph rules: gradient of a velocity-time graph is change in velocity divided by time, so it gives acceleration, and area under a velocity-time graph is velocity multiplied by time, so it gives displacement.
Therefore the statements about gradient giving acceleration, acceleration being rate of change of velocity, and area giving displacement are all correct.
Statement D says velocity is rate of change of distance, but distance is a scalar and its rate of change is speed, not vector velocity. Velocity must use vector displacement.

options.A: This is correct physics because gradient of velocity-time is $\Delta v / \Delta t$, which equals acceleration.
options.B: This is correct physics because acceleration is defined as $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$.
options.C: This is correct physics because area under velocity-time is velocity $\times$ time, which equals displacement.
options.D: This is not correct because velocity is the rate of change of displacement, while rate of change of distance is speed.
